items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: And my mom played piano and used to sing songs to me.

ctx.x: [coughs] pardon me. I hope there won’t be too much of that going on. I’ve got one of these California flu bugs or something. Oh, sure, you know, as we live life at the time, when we’re doing, like now what we’re doing, we think we’re doing the right thing for now. And I guess if you went back and looked at every now, you thought you were doing — I can see times when I probably could have done something a little differently, but I think on the whole, yeah, I’ve been very fortunate. Well the main thing I guess I’ve…

exposed to music, you know, from my mom and dad as a child. And see I have recollections of five and six you know, musical recollections. And so what are we talking about? Well ‘56 I did my first album, for Columbia Records. So we’re talking about 40 years, right in the middle of the whole thing, when you started hearing it. People thought in 1956, when my first album came out, like they think about everybody that becomes popular. “Wow, overnight guy here, where’s he been?” But as you think about it there have…
The songs that they were playing for you, they were probably considered popular music of that day, were they mostly vocal songs that they had, that you would sing along to?
